units.source_text: 我很喜欢佛典《盂兰盆经》里记载的日莲宗尊者

en.t: I am very fond of the story of the venerable figure of the Nichiren sect recorded in the Buddhist scripture Ullambana Sutra

units.source_text: （《盂兰盆经》内容记述的应该是佛陀之大弟子目连，

en.t: The Ullambana Sutra probably tells of Maudgalyayana, one of the Buddha's great disciples,

units.source_text: 因不忍其母堕饿鬼道受倒悬之苦，乃问法于佛，

en.t: who could not bear that his mother had fallen into the realm of hungry ghosts and was suffering as if suspended upside down, so he asked the Buddha for the Dharma,

units.source_text: 佛示之于七月十五日众僧自恣日，

en.t: and the Buddha instructed him that on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the day when the monks completed their confession and reflection,

units.source_text: 用百味饭食五果等供养十方佛僧，即可令其母脱离苦难。

en.t: if he made offerings of a hundred flavors of food, five kinds of fruit, and the like to the Buddhas and monks of the ten directions, he could free his mother from suffering.

units.source_text: 《盂兰盆经》，西晋三藏法师竺法护译。

en.t: The Ullambana Sutra was translated by the Western Jin Tripitaka master Dharmaraksha.

units.source_text: 日莲宗，日本佛教的主要宗派之一，由日莲上人在镰仓时代中期（约13世纪）所创立。）的故事。

en.t: Nichiren Buddhism is one of the major schools of Japanese Buddhism, founded by Saint Nichiren in the middle of the Kamakura period, around the thirteenth century.
There is also a story like this in the Sutra of Shanzi,

units.source_text: 记述道丕因为诵经的功德，

en.t: which records that through Daopi's merit from reciting scriptures,

units.source_text: 让他父亲的骷髅也跳起舞来了。

en.t: even his father's skeleton began to dance.

units.source_text: 我也很喜欢释迦牟尼世尊的前身——白象的故事。

en.t: I am also very fond of the story of the white elephant, a former incarnation of the World-Honored Shakyamuni.

units.source_text: 我觉得精灵祭从烧麻秆迎精灵开始到放河灯送鬼魂为止，

en.t: I think that the Bon festival, from burning hemp stalks to welcome the spirits to floating river lanterns to send off the souls of the dead,

units.source_text: 这种形式也是一种美好的过家家的游戏。

en.t: is, in this form, also a beautiful kind of make-believe game.
In order to make offerings to wandering ghosts,

units.source_text: 不会忘记超度河里的亡魂，

en.t: the Japanese do not forget to pray for the souls of the dead in the rivers,
and they even observe the festival of laying needles to rest.
